whatis.intro: Cost per delivery is the share of a route day that one stop uses up, whatever it carries. It comes from the day's driver, fuel and truck costs, split evenly across every drop. It is the cost a delivery minimum has to clear.

cards.title: Only the route day is counted
cards.body: The route day and nothing before it. Picking in the warehouse and the time spent taking the order sit outside the $27.18, so serving a stop costs more.
cards.alt: Plus sign, for the route costs a drop carries

cards.title: Every stop priced the same
cards.body: The calculator splits the day evenly, but a long unload or a detour uses more of the 8 hours than a quick drop.
cards.alt: Light bulb, for the difference between a long stop and a quick one

cards.title: The order that misses the route
cards.body: An order that arrives after the route is built waits a day or gets a trip of its own. A trip of its own puts driver time, fuel and the truck behind one drop.
cards.alt: Warning sign, for an order that arrives after the route is built

who.h2: Who uses a delivery cost calculator
who.intro: Any distributor running its own trucks can use it, from a single route to a full fleet. Whoever sets the delivery minimum, quotes a new stop or cuts a route should have that figure.

look.h2: Count the whole route day in the drop cost
look.intro: Driver cost is most of the day, so two of these checks start with the driver. The third is the miles.

steps.title: Hours from the timesheet
steps.body: Enter the hours the driver is paid, clock in to clock out, not just time on the road. If overtime is regular, build it into the hourly rate.

steps.title: A wage with the extras on
steps.body: $28.00 should carry payroll taxes, benefits and insurance, not just the pay rate. A bare wage makes every drop look cheaper than it is.

steps.title: Miles from yard to yard
steps.body: Use odometer miles for the whole day, out and back. Distance between stops on a map leaves out the run to the first drop and home again.

vos.h2: Where VOS sits before the route leaves
vos.h3: Orders can land before the route is built
vos.body: VOS does not plan routes, dispatch trucks or track deliveries. It works a step earlier. Customers order by voice in the VOS app, 24/7, and after-hours orders are in before the truck is loaded.
bullets: Each line reviewed by the customer before it is sent
For DSD, drivers show up with the right product
20-30 minutes saved per order compared with a phone order
vos.img_alt: Order review screen in the VOS app, listing each item and quantity before the order is placed

next.h2: What to run after cost per delivery
next.intro: A drop cost prices one stop. These three follow it to the next case, the building the cases ship from, and what they cost to bring in.

cards.title: See what your warehouse can hold
cards.body: Count how many cases your building holds once aisles and dock are out, and the weeks of flow that covers.
